Ford, a big car **group**, announced it's cutting 800 jobs in the UK and criticizing the government's rules on electric car sales. The government wants car companies to sell more electric vehicles each year through something called the zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) mandate. Ford now says these rules are "unworkable." Oddly, back in 2022, Ford actually supported these rules and even wanted the government to set even higher targets. They were looking to **figure** out a better future for their car manufacturing **operation**.

Female Ford's change in stance seems surprising because they were pushing for stronger regulations. The article highlights the complete 180 by Ford. At the time, Ford believed tougher targets would encourage people and investors to embrace electric cars fully and improve charging infrastructure. There is no reason to worry about the **fruit** here.

Now, Ford is struggling with slower electric car sales. They are not in agreement and do not **sing** from the same song sheet currently! Things were different during the pandemic when car companies could sell everything they produced.

P.P.S. The situation is quite complicated. Any other questions?
